newsitem.title: ITALY: Pope John Paul to get World Food Summit rolling.
newsitem.headline: Pope John Paul to get World Food Summit rolling.

text.p: Pope John Paul, a day after denouncing the "spectre of hunger", on Wednesday addresses some of the people best placed to resolve the problem.

The Pontiff gives the opening speech at a U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit expected to bring together around 100 heads of state and government ranging from Cuba's communist President Fidel Castro to free-market capitalist leaders.
United Nations Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali follows the Pope with a later address.

Castro's arrival, expected for early Friday, will undoubtedly add to the nightmare traffic congestion in central Rome as what is billed as the largest single peacetime security operation in Italy gets under way.
The five-day summit is being held at the Rome headquarters of the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) in a deliberate policy decision to prevent ostentatious spending.

Several thousand delegates and journalists will pace the maze-like corridors of the former "Ministry for an Italian Africa" built by Fascist dictator Benito Mussolini in 1935 as part of his grandiose but doomed colonial dreams.

For once, rare at such summits where haggling often continues to the last, the final texts have been agreed already -- allowing world leaders to concentrate on the global food situation over the five-day gathering.
They contain a specific pledge to reduce the number of undernourished people in the world to half the present level of 840 million by no later than the year 2015.
FAO director general Jacques Diouf said on the eve of the summit that the target to feed more than 400 million more people within 20 years was both "reasonable and achievable".
"We think we have a great chance of success provided...that the commitments made here are adhered to," Diouf said.
But the two main documents have faced criticism from development activists who say they are either utopian, too vague or little more than well-meaning words without muscle.

The summit will not seek hard cash pledges and is not scheduled to discuss answers to immediate crises, including the catastrophe in eastern Zaire where more than one million refugees from Rwanda and Burundi are at risk from fighting.

When the 76-year-old Pope, who knew hunger and hardship during World War Two as a young man in Poland, reads his opening address (0830 GMT) he is likely to call above all for compassion in a world in desperate need of it.

"The spectre of hunger and malnutrition is truly an offence against the Creator's image in every human being," the Pope told a group of non-governmental organisation representatives in a meeting at the Vatican on Tuesday.

Many of the NGOs are convinced supporters of using birth control and contraceptive measures, firmly opposed by the Roman Catholic Church, to ease hunger in a world expected to swell to 8.7 billion people in the year 2030 from 5.7 billion now.

Most of the leaders of the world's richest nations are not attending the summit. Only two of the so-called Group of Seven countries will be sending their prime ministers, with ministers representing the rest.
The United States, the world's biggest grain exporter, is sending Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman.
